reasons: The rule's preferred position is the absence of any non-solicit binding the Customer, so a document with no solicitation, no-hire, or inducement covenant correctly classifies as compliant rather than missing.

Cited paragraphs (§ 5.4 General Managers, § 10.2 No Joint Venture) contain no hiring or solicitation restraint, supporting the rationale; the exclusivity restraint noted binds the counterparty, not us, and is outside this rule's scope.

No redline or comment was proposed, which is the expected output for a compliant finding; the failed deterministic checks (duration, carve-out) simply reflect that no non-solicit clause exists to measure and do not indicate an error.
